messages:
julie: Hey team — first day! I completed Okta SSO and installed the VPN client, but I can't reach internal services (e.g., docker-registry.redwood.internal:5000) from my laptop. The client shows connected but DNS/requests time out. Any quick checks?

infra-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @julie! If this is onboarding VPN access please ping @maria for IT and @sam for network. See onboarding playbook: https://internal.redwood/onboarding/vpn (if you have access).

maria: Hi Julie — welcome! A couple quick things we usually verify:
1) Are you on company-managed device and marked as compliant in Okta? (disk encryption, OS patches)
2) Which OS? mac/linux/win?
3) Do you have the split-tunnel option enabled in the client? We push internal subnets, but some clients default to split-tunnel and don't route internal CIDRs.

julie: macOS Sonoma 14.2, personal laptop but enrolled in Okta device trust. Okta shows compliant. Where do I check split-tunnel?

maria: On the VPN client > Preferences > Network tab. If it says "Use system DNS" or "Split tunnel enabled" try toggling to "Route all traffic" temporarily. If that fixes it we can add the internal prefixes to the push list.

sam: Also confirm you're getting pushed routes for 10.10.0.0/16 and 10.20.0.0/16 (our internal VPCs). On mac you can run `netstat -rn | grep 10.` or `route -n get 10.10.0.1` to see the gateway. If there's no route, it's a client config issue.

julie: ran `netstat -rn | grep 10.` — nothing. VPN client shows connected, gateway 192.168.99.1 but doesn't list 10.10.0.0 route.

sam: OK that's split-tunnel. Workarounds:
- Temporary: enable "force tunnel" or "route all traffic" in the client (warn: slower internet).
- Longer term: I can add 10.10.0.0/16 and 10.20.0.0/16 to the push routes for your client profile. For that I need the VPN client version and the client profile ID.

julie: client: TunnelAgent 2.4.1, profile id: none shown in UI. How do I get profile id?

maria: If TunnelAgent doesn't show profile ID, upload the client logs to the onboarding ticket. For immediate unblock, Sam — can you suggest an SSH bastion path? I need her to get to the registry to pull a docker image for env setup.

sam: Sure — you can SSH via our bastion: `ssh -J julie@bastion.redwood.internal ubuntu@10.10.12.8` (replace ubuntu with your username on the target). That will hop through bastion and avoid needing full VPN routing for now.

julie: Trying `ssh -J julie@bastion.redwood.internal ubuntu@10.10.12.8` — it prompts for the YubiKey touch (I have one) then times out: "ssh: connect to host bastion.redwood.internal port 22: Connection timed out"

sam: Timeout suggests DNS not resolving bastion either. Two possibilities: corporate DNS isn't being used by split-tunnel. Try `dig bastion.redwood.internal @10.10.0.10` (10.10.0.10 is our internal DNS) — if that returns answer you're not using corporate DNS.

julie: `dig bastion.redwood.internal @10.10.0.10` -> connection timed out. `dig bastion.redwood.internal` -> NXDOMAIN.

maria: Hm. That indicates your client isn't able to reach the internal DNS server. Quick steps:
- Enable route-all in client to test.
- If you're on a personal laptop we require allowing split-tunnel but with specific internal routes. I'll open a VPN-onboard ticket to add the pushed routes for TunnelAgent 2.4.x and request network to check the DNS push.

maria: @sam can you add 10.10.0.0/16 and 10.20.0.0/16 to the TunnelAgent push list for profile family `onboard-2025` and confirm the DNS server 10.10.0.10 is included? Ticket: ONB-4523

sam: On it. I see `onboard-2025` has a split-tunnel template. I'll add the prefixes and push a policy. ETA 15–20m. I also pushed a temporary firewall exception for your user `julie@redwood` to allow SSH to bastion from your IP for 30m so you can finish the image pull.

julie: Thanks! I can SSH now but `docker pull docker-registry.redwood.internal:5000/repo/base:latest` hangs after TLS handshake.

sam: TLS handshake hang could be MTU or DNS cert. Try `curl -v https://docker-registry.redwood.internal:5000/v2/_catalog` to see TLS error. Also try reducing MTU: `sudo ifconfig utun0 mtu 1400` (temporary).

julie: `curl -v` shows SSL certificate for `registry.internal.redwood` (name mismatch).

maria: That indicates the registry cert uses an internal SAN; the hostname mismatch happens when split-tunnel + local DNS returns public name. If curl gives cert CN mismatch, try connecting to registry by IP `https://10.10.12.4:5000` as temp, or we'll add SAN for `docker-registry.redwood.internal`.

jordan: FYI, for onboarding we usually add a short-lived cert with SANs including `docker-registry.redwood.internal` to avoid this. I'll coordinate with infra PKI.

sam: Changes are live. You should now see 10.10 routes and DNS 10.10.0.10 pushed within ~2 mins. If not, restart the VPN client.

julie: Restarted VPN client -> `dig bastion.redwood.internal @10.10.0.10` now returns 10.10.1.5. SSH to bastion works, docker pull works via IP and by name. All good. Thank you all! :tada:

maria: Nice. Follow-up: Julie, I'll add you to the "VPN-Onboarded" Okta group so the policy persists and close ONB-4523. If you hit any other device compliance prompts ping me.

julie: Perfect. One last question — for future onboarding, is the recommended path company laptop > Okta managed? Or personal with device trust OK?

maria: Company laptop is recommended. Personal device with device trust works but has more manual steps (profile IDs, cert push). We'll add a short checklist to the onboarding doc to include client version and `netstat` output to speed up troubleshooting.

julie: Great — appreciate the quick help!
